newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover plunged to 2.4 billion yuan from 6.7 billion last Friday, with the 60-day contract the most active.

Traders said most rates fell, with trading volume shrinking today because many financial institutions reduced lending to ensure sufficient fund supply during the period before the Spring Festival in early February.

"It is normal that supply and demand tends to be unbalanced before and during the Spring Festival period," said one trader. "Some banks and other financial institutions held on to their funds and did less business today."

"A few financial institutions were short of money to settle accounts for the year-end and borrowed funds through short-term financial centres," said a second trader. "Their trade added liquidity to a dull market."
Traders believe rates will move in a tight range before the year-end, with no market-moving news in sight.
